*LATVIA*

# *Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied?* Yes
# *Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc)?* No
# *Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria?* No, there is no express presumption of employment. To establish the nature of the legal relationship, it is necessary to assess the nature of the obligations, the essential elements of employment may arise not only from the contract but also from the actual circumstances. A person may submit a claim to a court to recognize the service agreement as an employment contract. Any dispute about the nature of the contract must be settled by the court. Both parties must prove the facts on which they base their claims or objections. 
# *Are RSAs expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?* The main characteristic of the employment contract is the submission to the employer’s management and control - the employee complies with the employer’s rules and orders, and working time, whereas the employer ensures fair, safe and healthy working conditions.
# *Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?)* Yes, up to 2 years 
# *Who is able to take action against Bolt? Drivers / group action / regulators?* Drivers individually. If there are several identical cases against the same defendant, the court can consolidate them into a single proceeding, if it facilitates a more expeditious and correct resolution of the cases. Thus, each driver has to bring an action individually but may ask for his civil cases to be joined with other civil cases involving other drivers. 
Once the Directive is adopted, and after it is transported into the local law, it will become very likely that Labour or Tax authorities would use its ex-officio right to launch investigations into related subjects. The Directive will create a legal presumption of an employment relationship between platforms and persons performing platform work. Member States will be required to establish a framework for effective implementation of the legal presumption through appropriate measures, it will also mean strengthening controls and field inspections.
# *Is there any evidence the authorities have considered drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?* No
# *What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?* States fees are not high for claims that are not material (around EUR 70), and access to employment litigation is well established. If the court has already established employment relations, further employment-related claims are state fee free.
# *Can claims be made to reclassify all drivers of the platform in a market at once?* No. Court rulings have legal effect only for the parties of the dispute. So no court ruling on reclassification would be automatically applied to all the drivers who were not part of the proceeding. But the effect of a court precedent may trigger similar court actions.

*LITHUANIA* 

# *Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied?* Yes
# *Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc)?* No
# *Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria?* There is no express presumption of employment. 
# *Are RSAs expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?* 
To determine whether a _de facto_ employment relationship is formed, it is examined among other things if the person is under the subordination of the employer, complies with the employer's rules; if the employer takes the risk for the quality and timing of the person’s work. In the case of Bolt drivers there are many other attributes that lean towards civil relations such as the pay of the drivers depends on results, drivers take the risk for damages, plan their own work time, no workplace and tools are provided.
The totality of the circumstances is always assessed. The decision is made based on whether it is more likely that the relationship is in fact of employment.
# *Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?)* Yes, up to 3 years 
# *Who is able to take action against Bolt? Drivers / group action / regulators?* Drivers. Group action are permitted to defend public interest. However, private parties do not have a possibility to defend the public interest - this may be done only by a prosecutor or another authorized institution.
Once the Directive is adopted, and after it is transported into the local law, it will become very likely that Labour or Tax authorities would use its ex-officio right to launch investigations into related subjects. The Directive will create a legal presumption of an employment relationship between platforms and persons performing platform work. Member States will be required to establish a framework for effective implementation of the legal presumption through appropriate measures, it will also mean strengthening controls and field inspections.
# *Is there any evidence the authorities have considered drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?* No
# *What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?*  Access to employment litigation is well established. If the court has established employment relations, further employment-related claims are state fee free. 
# *Can claims be made to reclassify all drivers of the platform in a market at once?* No. Court rulings have legal effect only for the parties of the dispute. So no court ruling on reclassification would be automatically applied to all the drivers who were not part of the proceeding. But the effect of a court precedent may trigger similar court actions.

{code:sql}SELECT 
APPROX_DISTINCT(x.id,0.0041) AS count_all_requests,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.long_ride = 1 THEN x.id END,0.0041) AS count_long_ride_requests,
ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.long_ride = 1 THEN x.id END,0.0041)*1.0000/APPROX_DISTINCT(x.id,0.0041) AS double),4) AS long_ride_ratio,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.taxi_category = 1 THEN x.id END,0.0041) AS count_all_taxi_requests,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.long_ride = 1 AND x.taxi_category = 1 THEN x.id END,0.0041) AS count_long_ride_taxi_requests,
ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.long_ride = 1 AND x.taxi_category = 1 THEN x.id END,0.0041)*1.0000/APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.taxi_category = 1 THEN x.id END,0.0041) AS double),4) AS long_ride_taxi_ratio,
SUM(x.rejected_taxi_rule) AS count_rejected_by_rule
FROM (
SELECT
d.id,
d.meta.user_id AS user_id,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.order.search_category_id') AS category,
CASE WHEN json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.order.search_category_id') IN ('1313', '2514', '2870') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS taxi_category,
CASE WHEN cardinality (filter(d.strategies, x -> x.name = 'DE_TAXI_PREDICTED_LONG_RIDE_REJECT')) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS rejected_taxi_rule,

[~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2], there is one more important fact about Latvia which is not covered by questions but needs to be highlighted. No such issue in LT.

Latvian tax authority could rely on Article 8(2.2) of Personal income tax law according to which salary taxes must be paid by the company if the natural person (driver) meets at least *one* *criterion*. Bolt drivers meet one criterion _“Managed or controlled work, the person is not able to involve their own personnel or use sub-contractors”._ Thus, in practice, LV tax authorities already have a legal ground to claim payment of salary-related taxes for all the drivers, but such discussion/claim never took place in practice. 

Even if the Labour Inspection regards the relationship as non-employment, the tax authorities' assessment is made based on other legal provisions (Article 8(2.2) of Personal income tax) that consider different criteria than the Labour Inspection. Thus, *it is possible that LV tax authorities claim payment of salary-related taxes even if under the Labour law the drivers are not considered an employee.*

Notes about Anomaly detection project as discussed during today's meeting:

* Focus shifted from real-time predictions to daily predictions which allows to use more granular data from commerce orders etl table (especially about payment method and card_country features which is not stored in Grafana yet).
* I use Prophet model for time series prediction for selected metrics ({{gmv_eur, order_count, initial_failed_payment_count, initial_failed_payment_sum}}).
* An anomaly is identified when the true value of a metrics exceed 99% confidence interval of model prediction.
* 99% threshold is a value to adjust, so far I stick to this, but can change later.
* Model is evaluated with [cross validation|https://facebook.github.io/prophet/docs/diagnostics.html#:~:text=Prophet%20includes%20functionality%20for%20time,values%20to%20the%20actual%20values.]. This is done by selecting cutoff points in the history, and for each of them fitting the model using data only up to that cutoff point. We can then compare the forecasted values to the actual values.
* I analysed data for Rides UK from {{2022-03-01}} to {{2022-06-30}}. We had [fraud attack with Libyan cards there|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3915382892/2022-05-31+Fraud+-+Fraud+attack+with+Libyan+credit+cards], so I can play with model to check if it can identify this attack, not producing too many false positives.
* I tried several time aggregation: hourly, 3 hours, 6, hours, 12 hour and daily. The more frequent the data is, the more difficult for model to learn the trend for more granular data (1h data is ok for all Rides GMV in UK, but when looking specifically at french cards, there are lots of spikes here and there, which model predicts as anomalies - check the first screenshot below. Choosing bigger time intervals smooth the trend and makes model more accurate (second screenshot below). Good candidates so far are 12h and 1D based on data for card countries.
* Side note: Weather can influence hourly data and make it more fluctuating, like rain for example.
* We discussed what would be useful for analysts to see when receiving alerts about detected anomalies: all the info about specific data slice where anomaly is found (country, business line, payment method, card_country) and time period, like `2022-06-30 15:00 --2022-06-30 18:00) (if not daily aggregation of data - then we predict for the whole day).
* When we start receiving the alerts and understand more what to look at after seeing them, we can come up with a specific list of steps to check to simplify the work of analysts.

Next steps:

* Data cardinality: we have >180 unique card countries only in UK, making predictions for all of them doesn't make sense. I will experiment with adding {{other}} category: top-10 card-countries by volume and the others and validate that such cases as libyan cards can still be detected.
* More historical validation to estimate the amount of potential alerts.

{noformat}WITH a AS(
  SELECT
  	doub.user_id
  	, COUNT(DISTINCT doub.order_id) AS all_order_count
  	, MAX(CASE WHEN upu.first_market_vertical_purchase BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-30' AND DATE '2023-02-28' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS first_market
  	, MAX(CASE WHEN upu.first_vertical = 'Market' AND upu.first_market_vertical_purchase BETWEEN  DATE '2023-01-30' AND DATE '2023-02-28' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS market_first_bolt
  	, MAX(CASE WHEN upu.delivery_app_first_purchase = upu.first_market_vertical_purchase AND upu.delivery_app_first_purchase BETWEEN  DATE '2023-01-30' AND DATE '2023-02-28' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS market_first_delivery
  FROM ng_delivery.delivery_order_order AS doo
  LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.delivery_order_user_basket AS doub ON doub.order_id = doo.id
  LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.delivery_order_campaign AS doc ON doc.order_user_basket_id = doub.id
  LEFT JOIN ng_public.etl_user_products_usage AS upu ON doo.master_user_id = upu.user_id
  WHERE 
  	doc.code = '50EE'
  	AND doo.state = 'delivered'
  	AND doo.created_date BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-30' AND DATE '2023-02-28' 
  GROUP BY 1
)

SELECT
	SUM(all_order_count) AS total_order
	, COUNT(user_id) AS total_user_with_promocode
	, SUM(first_market) AS total_first_market_user
	, SUM(market_first_bolt) AS total_market_first_bolt
	, SUM(market_first_delivery) AS total_market_first_delivery
FROM a{noformat}

From [~accountid:62d7d51196f239ca6ae81612] 
”*B2B % in dispatch pool:*
in this query,
{{is_b2b_orders}} returns all drivers in the dispatching pool and whether they are {{b2b}} or not:

* {{order_id}} and {{city_id}} for order identification
* {{driver_id}}
* {{is_b2b}} whether this driver is in another order during dispatch

The last step in the query, just aggregates {{is_b2b}} wrt {{order_id}} and {{city_id:}}"


{noformat}WITH order_times AS (
-- Getting order start and end time (from driver accepted till order completely finished)
SELECT ot.order_id,
  ot.driver_id,
  a.created AS order_accept_time,
  b.created AS order_finish_time
FROM ng_public_spark.company_order_try ot
INNER JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try_state_log AS a 
      ON a.order_try_id = ot.id AND a.city_id = ot.city_id AND a.to_state = 'driver_accepted'
    INNER JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try_state_log b 
      ON b.order_try_id = ot.id AND b.city_id = ot.city_id AND b.to_state = 'finished'
WHERE TRUE
  AND ot.state = 'finished'
  AND ot.created_date = DATE('2023-01-09')
  AND a.created_date BETWEEN DATE('2023-01-09') AND DATEADD(DAY, 1, '2023-01-09')
  AND b.created_date BETWEEN DATE('2023-01-09') AND DATEADD(DAY, 1, '2023-01-09')
  
), is_b2b_orders AS (
-- for each order, get all drivers that were in the distaptching pool
-- and wether they were already in an another order when they received the request (is_b2b)
SELECT egr.order_id,
    eg.city_id,
    eg.created_date,
    egr.driver_id,
    (ti.order_id IS NOT NULL) as is_b2b
FROM geo.eta_getetas_route egr
    INNER JOIN geo.eta_getetas eg ON egr.eta_token = eg.eta_token
    LEFT JOIN order_times ti 
      ON egr.driver_id = ti.driver_id 
      AND egr.created_at BETWEEN ti.order_accept_time AND ti.order_finish_time
WHERE TRUE
    AND eg.requested_by_service = 'search_auto_order'
    AND egr.created_at_date BETWEEN DATE('2023-01-09') AND DATEADD(DAY, 1, '2023-01-09')
    AND eg.created_at_date = '2023-01-09'
)
-- Aggregating is_b2b in the dispatching pool for each order
SELECT bo.order_id, 
  bo.city_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_b2b THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*) AS dispatch_pool_b2b_rate
FROM is_b2b_orders bo
GROUP BY bo.order_id, bo.city_id{noformat}

From [~accountid:62d7d51196f239ca6ae81612] 
”*ETA error during drop-off leg (Drop-off en-route ETA error):*
We haven't discussed this one, but let me know if possible to add as well. Currently, we only measure the error end-to-end i.e. from pickup to drop-off. This query is measure the error for predictions that happen during the ride, for example midway from pick to drop-off.
It returns:

* {{order_id}} and {{city_id}} for order identification
* {{provider_version}} model version used
* {{actual_travel_time}}
* {{eta_error}} (signed)
* {{eta_error_abs}} (absolute)”

{noformat}WITH no_interim_steps AS (
  SELECT
      order_try_id,
      COUNT (CASE WHEN stop_type = 'arrival' THEN id END) AS interim_stops

  FROM ng_public_spark.company_order_try_route_log corl
  -- buffer to make sure joins are not destructive
  WHERE corl.created BETWEEN DATEADD(HOUR, -1, '2023-02-22') AND DATEADD(HOUR, 25, '2023-02-22')
      AND corl.created_date BETWEEN DATEADD(DAY, -2, '2023-02-22') AND DATEADD(DAY, 2, '2023-02-22')
      AND corl.stop_type <> 'change_point'
      AND corl.order_try_state = 'driving_with_client'

  GROUP BY order_try_id
  -- Remove rides with multiple stops
  HAVING interim_stops = 0
), dropoff_leg_times(
SELECT
    ot.id AS order_try_id,
    ot.order_id,
    ot.city_id,
    ot.driver_id,
    ots_a.created as dropoff_start_time,
    ots_b.created as dropoff_end_time,
    unix_timestamp (ots_a.created) AS dropoff_start_timestamp,
    unix_timestamp (ots_b.created) AS dropoff_end_timestamp,
    ot.state

FROM ng_public_spark.company_order_try ot
    JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try_state_log AS ots_a ON ots_a.order_try_id = ot.id AND ots_a.city_id = ot.city_id 
        AND ots_a.to_state = 'driving_with_client'
    JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try_state_log AS ots_b ON ots_b.order_try_id = ot.id AND ots_b.city_id = ot.city_id 
        AND ots_b.to_state = 'arrived_to_destination'
    JOIN no_interim_steps nos ON ot.id = nos.order_try_id

WHERE ot.state = 'finished'
    AND ot.created_date = DATE('2023-02-22')
    AND ots_a.created_date BETWEEN DATE('2023-02-22') AND DATEADD(DAY, 1, '2023-02-22')
    AND ots_b.created_date BETWEEN DATE('2023-02-22') AND DATEADD(DAY, 1, '2023-02-22')
    -- Include normal orders only
    AND ot.search_algorithm in ('normal')
    AND ot.id IS NOT NULL
    AND ot.city_id IS NOT NULL
    AND unix_timestamp(ots_a.created) IS NOT NULL
    AND unix_timestamp(ots_b.created) IS NOT NULL
    AND ots_a.lat IS NOT NULL
    AND ots_a.lng IS NOT NULL
    AND ots_b.lat IS NOT NULL
    AND ots_b.lng IS NOT NULL
)

SELECT 
  dlt.order_id,
  dlt.city_id,
  dlt.driver_id,
  
  egrs.provider_version,
  egrs.created_at AS segment_start_time, 
  dlt.dropoff_start_time, 
  dlt.dropoff_end_time,
  
  dropoff_end_timestamp - unix_timestamp(egrs.created_at) AS actual_travel_time,
  egrs.duration_from_strategy,
  egrs.duration_from_strategy - (dropoff_end_timestamp - unix_timestamp(egrs.created_at)) AS eta_error,
  ABS(egrs.duration_from_strategy - (dropoff_end_timestamp - unix_timestamp(egrs.created_at))) AS eta_error_abs
  
FROM geo.eta_getetas_route_segment egrs
  INNER JOIN geo.eta_getetas_route egr
    ON egrs.eta_token = egr.eta_token AND egrs.route_no = egr.route_no
  INNER JOIN geo.eta_getetas eg
    ON egr.eta_token = eg.eta_token
  INNER JOIN dropoff_leg_times dlt ON dlt.order_id = egr.order_id AND dlt.city_id = eg.city_id AND dlt.driver_id = egr.driver_id
      -- This clause is to fix rows where driving to dropoff is before pickup. Not sure how this happens.
      AND  egrs.created_at BETWEEN dlt.dropoff_start_time AND dlt.dropoff_end_time
  
WHERE TRUE
  AND eg.created_at_date = DATE('2023-02-22')
  AND egr.created_at_date BETWEEN DATE('2023-02-22') AND DATEADD(DAY, 1, '2023-02-22')
  AND egrs.created_at_date BETWEEN DATE('2023-02-22') AND DATEADD(DAY, 1, '2023-02-22')

  AND from_action = 'driver_location'
  AND to_action = 'dropoff'
  AND egrs.provider = 'internal'
  AND eg.requested_by_service IN ('rides-routing-cron', 'rides-routing'){noformat}

Hi [~accountid:5afe99c869aa3d30612279da] as requested, please find the feedback here. To a large extent this is nothing new - but see section C and the text I have put in bold re the potential risk on us. Please let me know if you have any follow-up questions? 

_A. Introduction_

 _Platform operations are not specifically regulated in Cyprus. The current regulatory framework in Cyprus applies at the level of taxi drivers and their vehicles, which are heavily regulated. As far as we are aware, in practice, the Cyprus Department of Road Transport of the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Works (the “Department of Road Transport”) treats taxi platforms in the same way as taxi companies and expects them to ensure compliance by drivers with the legislation that governs the operation of taxis in Cyprus._

_B. Liability at the taxi driver’s level_

 _i) Professional Taxi Licence_

_Taxi drivers must hold a professional taxi driver’s licence as prescribed by the Professional Driver's Licence of 2011 (L.80(I)/2011) (as amended) (the “Professional Driver’s Licence Law”)._

_ii) Road usage licence_

_In addition, pursuant to section 14 of the Law on the Regulation of Traffic Transport of 1982 (L.9/1982) (as amended) (the “Traffic Transport Law”), it is prohibited for any person to transport passengers for hire or for a fee with a private motor vehicle. A motor vehicle for public use, such as a taxi, would have to be used. A motor vehicle may be used as a taxi only if a road usage licence has been issued in respect of that vehicle, in accordance with section 5 of the Traffic Transport Law, for one of the following uses: (a) urban taxi service; or (b) rural taxi service or (c) intercity taxi service. In order to work as a taxi driver, one can either obtain such a licence for their own vehicle or rent a vehicle that already has such a licence._

_The authority responsible for granting such road usage licences is the licensing authority of the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Works (the “Licensing Authority”)._

_To the extent that the above requirements are not complied with by companies such as InDrive and Alfa Cyprus, they would be operating in violation of the applicable legislation._

_iii) Dynamic Pricing_

_Pursuant to section 9 of the Traffic Transport Law, urban taxis must be fitted with a taximeter and charge the amount displayed by the taximeter at the end of the ride. As such, urban taxi drivers cannot charge a fixed fare at the beginning of the ride or offer discounted prices or promotions._

_Taxi drivers can have their professional taxi driver’s licence or road usage licence for their vehicles suspended or revoked by the Licensing Authority for violating the Professional Driver’s Licence Law or the Traffic Transport Law. In addition, they can be subject to other disciplinary action, including the imposition of a monetary fine, for violation of the above laws._

_Criminal liability may also apply for taxi drivers who violate the provisions of the above laws (e.g. for driving a taxi without the appropriate road usage licence or for violating the conditions of such licence or the provisions of the Traffic Transport Law)._

_iv) Liability at the platform operator’s level_

_Pursuant to section 21 of the Traffic Transport Law, any person who uses a motor vehicle or_ *_causes, allows or tolerates_* _the use of such vehicle in contravention of such law, or any of the regulations issued pursuant to such law, can be found criminally liable and subject to imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months and/or to a fine not exceeding EUR 768. In addition, if a person is found guilty of the above offence by a court, and consequently refuses to comply or does not comply with such court order, he/she/it may be found guilty of a criminal offence and may be subject to imprisonment for a period not exceeding one year and/or to a fine not exceeding EUR 1,710._

_Thus,_ *_potential liability for Bolt may arise under the above-mentioned section 21 of the Traffic Transport Law if, by facilitating the provision of taxi services through its platform, Bolt is found by a court to have_* +*_caused, allowed or tolerated_*+ *_the use of a vehicle by a taxi driver or a non-taxi driver in contravention of the relevant law (e.g. by introducing dynamic pricing_*_)._

_C. Risk assessment_

_Therefore, Bolt may be found liable pursuant to section 21 of the Traffic Transport Law, as mentioned above. Such penalties would only be imposed following a conviction in court._

_D. Market knowledge_

_From previous correspondence with the Department of Road Transport, we understand that in the past there have been complaints regarding non-compliance by taxi drivers operating via a platform, e.g. concerning failure to use the taximeter or to charge according to the prescribed fares, and that such complaints have been raised by the authorities with the intermediary platforms concerned. Our understanding is that letters were sent by the relevant authorities to the management of such intermediary platforms requesting those platforms to stop such practices and take down the various offered prices or promotions from their websites. Some intermediate platforms complied with the request and some did not. In response, the Licensing Authority reported the matter to the Cypriot police and the Law Office of the Republic of Cyprus._

_Please note that we are not aware of any court decisions relating to the above. As such, we are not in a position to know the outcome of these investigations (whether they were dropped or settled in some manner or whether any penalties were imposed)._

SELECT

    SUM(final_table.users) as users_count,

    SUM(final_table.cost) as costs,
    SUM(final_table.impressions) as impressions,
    SUM(final_table.clicks) as clicks,
    SUM(final_table.cost) * 1 / (1-COALESCE(cannibalisation, 0.05)) as cannibalisation_costs,
    SUM(sum_1y_profit_simplified_eur) AS profit_simplified_eur,
    SUM(sum_1y_gmv_eur) AS gmv_eur,
    current_timestamp() AS _last_ingested

FROM

LEFT JOIN

ON

    AND final_table.channel_name = cannibalisation_table.channel_name
    AND final_table.os = cannibalisation_table.os

{% if is_incremental() %}

Art. 58 says:

(1) The Taxpayer/Payer or another person authorised by him has the obligation to provide the fiscal body with the necessary information to determine the fiscal status. For the same purpose, the fiscal body has the right to request information *from other persons with whom the taxpayer/payer has or had economic or legal relations, and they have the obligation to provide the requested information.* The information provided by other persons is taken into account only to the extent that it is also confirmed by other means of proof.

(2) The request for the provision of information shall be made in writing. In the request, the fiscal body must specify the nature of the information requested to determine the fiscal status and the documents that support the information provided, when they are not held by the fiscal body.

(3) Declaration of persons obliged according to para. (1) to provide information will be, as the case may be, presented or recorded in writing.

(4) In the event that the person obliged to provide the information in writing is, for reasons independent of his will, unable to write, the fiscal body draws up a report.

The performance test I run uses keep alive connection with the *raster* service. At the moment raster service calls the vector k8s service directly (previously the communication was via ALB, but no changes in behaviour is seen now).Whenever the number of raster services is greater than 1 issue starts manifesting through very high latency (at regular cadence, during this time CPU drops with with respect to decreased load).With the current *raster* configuration, one instance is capped at ~200requests/s (it is a node service calling some native lib, scaling vertically does not help). Scaling horizontally (tried running 2,4 and 8 raster pods) increases the load up to ~400 request/s but we end up having latency issues (to me it looks like load balancer spill over), and the more raster services we have the periods with high latency gets more frequent.All the pods are not reaching CPU/Memory bounds.Attaching the performance metrics I got (I do not remember the initial set-up, this is the reason I did not annotate it).

As per sre recommendation I tried to set-up the osm-raster and osm-vector-nginx to run inside the same pod and communicate on localhost, unfortunately with this set-up raster starts behaving weird (software issue), it sais it gets empty vector tiles from vector-nginx (but it actually does not invoke it as there are no access logs on vector-nginx side) and cannot create png tiles. The said part is that sometimes it properly makes the calls and it manages to create raster tiles in the end. 

I tried also collocation osm-raster with osm-vector inside the same pod and communicate directly without vector-nginx, same issues reoccur (but in this set-up it looks that raster tiles are more often created with success). What is  more weird is that after one deployment I had everything working as expected, and after another one things did not work (with no code changes, just rebuild the images).

Taking into consideration the previous comment, the most stable and low latency is when we have a single raster instance, also deployed just one vector-nginx instance (we will benefit better from the cache reutilisation for subsequent raster calls for the same vector tiles).

If 200 tps/s will not be enough we may deploy 2 raster instances, however periodically there will be higher latencies. (Unfortunately, scaling further does not make any sence as the max tps does not increase but the latency degrades)

Web scraping is a process that automatically load, read and extract data from websites using software tools known as web scrapers or web crawlers. 

h3. Overview

* Got familiar with web scraping process
* Did a research how to scrape a web page and what are the required tools
* Installed Python (programming language)
* Installed Visual Studio Code (code editor tool)
* Installed Scrapy (software tool for crawling websites)
* Get used with Scrapy by following the tutorial

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
I managed to extract some text lines from a static website into a .CSV 
{panel}

*Static website:* [https://quotes.toscrape.com/|https://quotes.toscrape.com/|smart-link] 

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
I tried to extract some road closure info from one of our sources, which is a dynamic website, but didn’t succed.
{panel}

*Dynamic website:* [https://viz.berlin.de/verkehr-in-berlin/baustellen-und-sperrungen/|https://viz.berlin.de/verkehr-in-berlin/baustellen-und-sperrungen/|smart-link] 

h3. Conclusion

When web crawling might be two cases:

* Crawling static pages (the data remains the same)
* Crawling dynamic pages (the data constantly changes)

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
Crawling dynamic pages could be more difficult and implies advanced coding knowledge.

Most of our road closure sources are stored in dynamic pages.
{panel}



h3. The good part

Some of the websites could make a request to an URL which downloads the data in a JSON format which can be loaded and visualised in Atlas and afterwards converted to a Geojson for further GIS analyses.

JSON format: [https://api.viz.berlin.de/daten/baustellen_sperrungen.json|https://api.viz.berlin.de/daten/baustellen_sperrungen.json]

Hey Julius,

Billing team uses the balance while generating the invoice. And every time there is a new invoice generation request (download), the system takes the current balance for this period and generates the invoice. By this logic, invoices are bound to change as local operations teams are retrospectively doing manual adjustments. If, on March 03, you manually add a compensation to a driver’s balance for January 01 in the amount of 100€, January invoice will display 100€ more in balance when you download it later.

So, as long as we have retrospective corrections (be it manual adjustments, or technical corrections) which we are also obligated to do, this has to happen. If there is a local regulation suggesting we shouldn’t under any circumstances, I recommend you discuss this with Legal team and open a ticket [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/61/create/301] for such a logic change (including the impact calculation such as fees we might have to pay, or possible loss of license, amount of drivers complaining etc.)

Overall, although we charge the commission from cash rides, we don’t display these cash rides in the balance but we show the commission for those. So, it might be causing confusion to see more commission for the day - but that’s because we don’t display the cash as they already have it.

Hi [~accountid:6052891960d39e006f72f0f0], please find below answers to your questions:

*CROATIA*

# *Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied? yes/no*
## yes, starting from 1.1.2024.
# *Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc)*
## yes, new legislation that becomes effective on 1.1.2024. will regulate platform work. Furthermore, recently the platform worker unions started protesting and requesting the government to regulate platform work even stricter than was planned. They are requesting the right to become platforms' employees and the right to influence their earnings for the work provided using the platform.
# *Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria? yes/no*
## yes.
# *Are reclassification sensitive activity expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?*
## not yet
# *Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?)*
## yes, for the period of 3 years preceding the date of filing a claim
# *Who is able to take action against Bolt? couriers / group action / regulators*
## everyone with a legitimate interest can file a claim before the court against Bolt requesting the court to assess whether the relationship between Bolt and the courier is an employment relationship. The new legislation (which enters into force on 1.1.2024.) does not prescribe any fines or penalties for platforms that are not compliant with the new regulation, however, it prescribes platforms' *joint and several liabilities* for the payment of the couriers' salaries and employment benefits in case aggregators (fleets) do not pay them. Platforms can be released of this liability in case they can prove that they have been requesting aggregators on a monthly basis, proof that all salaries have been paid to all fleet employees.
# *Is there any evidence the authorities have considered drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?*
## no
# *What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?*
## Overall, while there is room for improvement, Croatia's legal system generally provides a reasonable level of access to justice. Legal fees are reasonable, and there is no requirement to have a legal representative i.e. parties can represent themselves or can be represented by an employee who has a bar exam. However, there are still some challenges with the length of court proceedings in Croatia. In some cases, the backlog of cases can result in significant delays, and it could take years for the case to be resolved.
# *Can claims be made to reclassify all couriers of the platform in a market at once?*
## No, only the ones who would participate in a court proceeding and to whom the final judgment applies to. In case of claims raised by unions/group of couriers, the judgment would apply only to their members.
## The regulators could reclassify all couriers by passing new legislation, but at this moment there is no sign they plan to do so.

Please let me know in case you have any questions or need any clarifications.

BR,

Iva

[https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/metrics|https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/metrics|smart-link] 

There is a whole framework in dbt to create metrics! 

They show up as separate items in the dependency graphs:

!image-20230410-092657.png|width=2772,height=1316!

It even has logic for non-aggregatable metrics: [https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/metrics#derived-metrics|https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/metrics#derived-metrics|smart-link] 

Requires [https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt_metrics|https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt_metrics|smart-link] package. 

One can also return multiple metrics with one query: [https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt_metrics#multiple-metrics|https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt_metrics#multiple-metrics|smart-link] 



From [https://stkbailey.substack.com/p/kicking-the-tires-on-dbt-metrics|https://stkbailey.substack.com/p/kicking-the-tires-on-dbt-metrics|smart-link] 

The basic pattern is:

* Build a single high-quality fact table with the necessary dimensions and time columns
* Define the desired metrics in YAML
* [Materialize the metrics|https://github.com/stkbailey/streamlit-dbt-metrics-explorer/blob/main/example_dbt_project/models/netflix/netflix_release_metrics.sql], including any secondary calculations, in a new model using the metrics macro
* Optionally, join or union many of these materializations into a single model

*BOLT*: We have added following clauses:

9.2: _“Bolt will agree to compensate the Agency for any direct or indirect loss or damage arising from or in connection with the breach of the Agreement.”_

9.4 _“The liability for each Party under the Agreement is limited to the value of applicable SOW.”_

*Under “Indemnification” please add a clause that in order to protect the brand image of both Bolt and The Agency, should the comment section of the content across platforms become too defamatory in nature to either party, both parties agree that the comment section of said post(s) may be limited to protect said brand images.*

*BOLT*: In this regard, we have added clause 6.3 in the following wording_: “The Parties agree to cooperate in good faith to find the best solution to protect each other’s brand and reputation should the comments regarding Talent Materials and related content become too defamatory to either Party.“_

*-An Ownership Clause which specifies that Bolt will have limited ownership of the content limited to the duration of the agreed upon usage rights. *BOLT*: this is essentially written in clause 5.1 “_The licence is deemed to be given to Bolt now of the creation of such content. The license is valid for the entire duration of the respective rights agreed by the Parties in applicable SOW_.„ The legal meaning of the licence is that the ownership belongs to either Talent (or other third party) and Bolt only receives license to use the material for the duration and in the channels and in the territories listed in the SOW. {noformat}with tmp as (
select date(co.created_date) created_date
      ,co.user_id 
      ,co.price_currency as currency
      ,count(DISTINCT co.order_id) as debt_orders
      ,SUM(co.user_price) debt_sum
      ,SUM(co.uncovered_amount) current_debt
      ,SUM(co.user_price-co.uncovered_amount) recovered
      ,SUM(co.bolt_credit_captured_amount) bolt_credit_captured_amount
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co
WHERE co.created_date >= date '2023-01-01' 
AND co.order_type = 'rides'
AND co.payment_method_group = 'bolt_credit'
AND (co.payment_method_id = 'cash' OR (co.payment_method_id = 'card' AND co.country_code = 'nl'))
AND co.user_price_eur > 0
AND co.order_state <> 'finished'
--and co.user_id = 1643966
group by 1,2,3
),
recovery AS (
select 
entity_id,
currency,
created_date,
surplus_current_balance,
deficit_current_balance,
case when surplus_current_balance + deficit_current_balance < 0 then 'in_debt' else 'debt_cleared' end as debt_status,
lag(created_date) over(partition by entity_id, currency, deficit_current_balance order by created_date desc) as date_shifted
from ng_public_spark.etl_billing_debt_user_v2 
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6
order by created_date desc
), 
payment_info as (
select
entity_id as user_id,
currency,
deficit_current_balance,
created_date as debt_created,
date_shifted as payment_date_v1,
coalesce(date_shifted, last_value(date_shifted) IGNORE nulls OVER(order by entity_id, currency, created_date rows between current row and 1 following)) as payment_date
from recovery
where debt_status = 'in_debt'
group by 1,2,3,4,5
order by created_date desc
),
overview as (
select tmp.*,
      case when tmp.recovered = 0 then null --> user still in debt
        when tmp.recovered > 0 and pin.payment_date is null then tmp.created_date --> user paid the debt in the same day
        else pin.payment_date end as debt_payment_date --> otherwise the payment date
from tmp 
left join payment_info pin on tmp.created_date = pin.debt_created and tmp.user_id = pin.user_id and tmp.currency = pin.currency
)

select *
from overview
where debt_payment_date > created_date
limit 100{noformat}

I’ve explored a few methods for this problem and ended up using K-Nearest Neighbors classification algorithm. The outcome is a significantly smaller set of users (from 75K -> 4.3K) with no selection bias - users in control are similar to those who have subscribed in the treatment groups. I’ve sent the source code and dataset to Priit so he could continue with comparisons against control. From a quick glance I see there is positive lift in metrics between control & treatments.

[Detail on modeling|http://datascience.internal/rider_campaigns/bolt-plus/bolt_plus_lift.html] ([link to code|https://github.com/bolteu/data-science-research/blob/main/campaigns-rider/bolt-plus/bolt_plus_lift.ipynb]):
_K-nearest neighbour is a supervised ML algorithm that assumes similarity between the feature space and output category - in our case similarity between user historical features before experiment started and the subscription action as a result. We apply this algorithm for each treatment group separately with k = 1 to choose the single nearest neighbour. At the end we predict with each KNN model and combine the predictions by selecting users for whom any of the KNN models predicted that he/she will subscribe._

+*TAXABLE SUPPLY.*+

# Public fines arising from the infringement of local traffic authorities do not qualify as a taxable supply subject to VAT. These fines fall out of the scope of VAT, so Bolt does not have to charge VAT to the user and does not have to issue an invoice to charge the fine to the user.
# Contractual penalties arising from a breach of the terms and conditions qualify as a service subject to VAT (a taxable supply) ONLY if the penalty qualifies as the consideration of a service provided to the user (i.e, cleaning a vehicle, towing a vehicle back within a designated area, administration and management of public fines, etc). In this case, Bolt must charge output VAT to the user and must do so through an invoice.
# Contractual penalties charged to compensate Bolt for damages and/or losses fall out of the scope of VAT. We don’t have to charge output VAT on these amounts, and we don’t have to provide the user with an invoice to charge these amounts.

+*APPLY VAT*+

a.             VAT standard rates are included in the matrix shared through Slack.

b.             Agnostic logic.

i.       Determine the place of supply (for rentals: the country where the equipment was rented, even if the supplier is a foreign entity).

Short-term (less than 30 days) rental of vehicles (both micro-mobility electric vehicles and cars) are subject to VAT in the country where the vehicle is put at the users’ disposal.

ii.       Who should be taxed (seller or buyer or neither)?

This question does not apply in the case at hand. The VAT taxpayer of a rental business activity (both the rental of micro-mobility electric vehicles or the rental of cars) is the company providing the rental service as the principal service provider.

In our case, the VAT taxpayer is Bolt Ops OÜ in countries where we provide rental services under the standard business model, or the local entities in countries where we provide rental services (micro-mobility or car-sharing) under the localized business model.

Either Bolt Ops or the Bolt local entity must charge VAT to the users on the gross rental fee and, in principle, are entitled to deduct input VAT.

iii.     VAT rate.

Micro-mobility rental services and car-sharing services are always subject to the VAT standard rate provided for by the VAT regulations in force in each one of the countries where we operate this business activity.

Should you require further information or any clarification please let me know.

Thank you! Have a good day.

All authenticated endpoints use {{user-auth/internal/auth}} endpoint to check credentials ({{phone}} and {{phone_uuid}} from {{Authorization}} header).
This method is in charge to find the user_id associated to the provided phone and device_uuid info. We look first in the cache({{user_auth_node_cache}}), and if we don’t find it, we check it in the db table({{user_login}}). In case the login token is expired we throw an error({{ResponseCodes.USER_LOGIN_EXPIRED}})
**The cache expire time is currently set to 2 mins.

In order to support the log out functionality we need the following:

* exposing an *external* *authenticated* *endpoint* for logout that would receive the phone and phone_uuid info
* deleting the associated cache record for the token
* setting expire time for the token to NOW in the db table



Extra (to be considered):

** Old app versions are calling {{/user/v1/identify/phone}} / {{/user/v1/identify/phone}} which will set an expire time of 1 hour if it finds an existing login token and adds a new login token

Also in the future we might want to expose the functionality in admin or have some other security crons that would help with this.

* we can add an expiration_source column in the table and log this data when we are firing {{ResponseCodes.USER_LOGIN_EXPIRED}} error so we have more context when we see this error increase.

From my side - currently all driver’s pictures are taken in the HUB when they register and we would like to keep it so. Here is the methodology we launched: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/17p7di_6cr-xDO3r_VK7JWSwTpbarmzauACyTJzXOZmk/edit#heading=h.c9p5szxxk3db|https://docs.google.com/document/d/17p7di_6cr-xDO3r_VK7JWSwTpbarmzauACyTJzXOZmk/edit#heading=h.c9p5szxxk3db|smart-link] There is also section about legal risk in the methodology. For determining the legal framework the legal council should do following:

* Country legal council  uses [+Legal questionnaire+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-ZjNVX9rtsXA4IWpYt5PR3RVGLfNBY46OdpE7JGvy5g/edit] and checks following: 
** criminal punishment scope for specific country
** civil punishment scope for specific country 
** competitor T&C review
** etc
* Country legal council uses answers to questionnaire to define punishment scope for each window shopping scenario in the [+global risk matrix+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_eWb4mN9Nph8g1OuD0urnNoYmaPGjHEwlKYIMw3KfCU/edit]:
** Punishment scope will be considered every time. But if the  likelihood of the risk materializing is *LOW* than we will not ask about punishment.

Hi [~accountid:60f2a71843c956007065f2ad] the advice from the external has been shared with the privacy team and I believe - taken into account in the proposed response. One of the external’s recommendation was to request a more attainable timeline, given the complexity of the request, and also to substantiate the relevance of the data by the police. 



Sharing the full advice again for the visibility. 

* *What is the legal framework for the police to send a data requests to Bolt? is Criminal Code / Code of Criminal Procedure a sufficient legal basis for the police to this end?*

The legal provisions indicated by the police indeed represent the legal framework for requesting documents and data, as well as applicable sanctions i.e. (art. 170, para. (1) Criminal Procedure Code, art. 170, paragraph (2), letter a) Criminal Procedure Code). They refer to the general obligation to cooperate with law enforcement in the case of a criminal investigation.Non compliance with such a request can under certain conditions be qualified as a criminal offence (art. 271 para. (1) lit. b of the Criminal Code). We analyzed this offence further within the answer to question 4 below.Interestingly, in this particular case, it is arguable whether a fine could be applied to Bolt. Art. 283 para. (4) lit. d) from the Code of Criminal Procedure, cited as legal basis, does not cover the handing over of data, but only documents and specific objects. Thus, applying it to non-delivery of data would mean adding new rules to an existing law, which is not permitted. Simply put, the Parliament did not correlate Art. 283 para. (4) lit. d) with art. 170 of the Criminal Procedure Code, leaving an unintended legal gap.2. - does GDPR limitations apply here? are there any local specifics we should take into account?This situation is regulated by both the GDPR and Directive (EU) 2016/680 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data by competent authorities for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties, and on the free movement of such data, transposed in Romania by Law no. 363/2018.Under Law no. 363/2018, the police have the legal right to process personal data related to criminal law enforcement, including the categories of data requested from Bolt. Nonetheless, the police are also subject to the obligation for personal data processing to be lawful, i.e. necessary for the performance of a task carried out by a competent authority. This obligation mirrors the GDPR, meaning that Bolt is only obligated to provide such information which is necessary and [proportionate. To|http://proportionate.to/] comply with the necessity principle, Bolt is only required to provide as much personal data as is adequate, relevant and limited to the purpose of sharing with the police. Bolt needs to be satisfied that the personal data is necessary for the police to fulfil its law enforcement purpose, as such Bolt may ask the police to what extent the information requested is necessary.Nonetheless, the mere volume of information is not an adequate reason not to provide it. Therefore, if Bolt is satisfied that the information is necessary in relation to an ongoing investigation, then the information should be disclosed.

* *- is Bolt obliged to provide the information in case of such a broad scope as in the case at hand?*

The law provides in general terms the purpose of the data request. The police/prosecution is entitled to request any data they have reason to believe it might serve to solve the case, without limitation in volume.

As also mentioned under point 2 above, there is a condition of relevance. The police need to have sound reasoning to believe that the information they request could potentially help them. In other words, there needs to be some sort of logic / legitimate interest for wanting a certain type of information.

In the specific case, the police request itineraries for rides. You are correct in saying that this does not seem to have any connection with illegal access of computer systems and fraudulent financial operations.

However, there may be a reasonably legitimate interest, e.g. identifying the suspects. Hence, it is legitimate for the police to request information that can lead to the capture of the culprit. The itineraries might indicate their travels to and from their home, work place, hang outs etc.

* *What are the consequences for Bolt/the management/ the employees - do the provisions mentioned by the policy indeed apply?*

As mentioned above, Bold might not face a fine, due to lack of legislation, but could be charged with a criminal offence under certain conditions.

Obstruction of justice requires:

* a criminal file to open and under pending investigation – which is the case;
* a refusal to comply with the data request – either explicit or implicit; Explicit means telling them directly that you refuse to give them the data. It is irrelevant if the noncompliance is for all or part of the data. In your case you tried to negotiate at first, but after the police gave you a clear answer that you need to give all data, any further attempts to avoid giving them data could be interpreted as an implicit refusal (i.e. that you stick to you original position of only offering 10 itineraries); Therefore, best to avoid any such discussion in the further. You could try to ask for more time, which should not be considered a refusal at first.
* the data request must be explicit and within the applicable legal framework – which is the case;
* there needs to be a prior warning from the legal authority in respect of the consequences for non-compliance with the data request – which is also the case – the police told you that you might face criminal charges if you do not provide the data.

In conclusion, further refusing to comply could expose Bolt to a potential charge. This could affect Bolt or its employees, depending on who actually refuses to cooperate (it will be determined whether it was a corporate decision or an individual one).

* *We want to understand if we have any push-back solutions here? The options to force the police to narrow down the request?*

The ordinances issued within a criminal investigation can be challenged through a formal challenge. The challenge against the ordinances of the police are solved by the case prosecutor. Such a challenge could be taken into consideration if for example there is no clear legitimate interest for the data request, or the conditions for the request are not met.

A second solution would be for Bolt Services RO to claim that it does not have access or control over the data requested and that the data is under the control of an entity outside Romanian jurisdiction. However, given that up to this point Bolt has complied with the request, this would probably not be the best solution and would only antagonize the authorities.

In the case at hand, it is probably best to obtain a more attainable timeline, given the complexity of the request. In addition, we could also ask for the police to substantiate the relevance of the data, and escalate the matter to the case prosecutor. However, given that the criminal investigation is confidential, it will be very difficult to actually demonstrate the data is irrelevant or too broad.

The UTF-8 (Unicode Transformation Format with 8-bit units) method for encoding Unicode data is implemented according to RFC 3629, which describes encoding sequences that take from one to four bytes. You are correct, digits will only use one byte, thus the revised estimation would be:

Increase from 8->18bytes =10 * 775160497 rows = 7751604970 bytes =~7.75GB increase

One question remains, why change from BIGINT to VARCHAR? Do you expect to have alphanumeric rows in future?

{quote}I’d like to understand better what does it mean that it’s be operationally expensive: is this mosty about waiting time (we’d have to wait a long time for the table to be replicated), or would it incur some other cost/require some more work?{quote}

It means that altering large tables online implies using tools like gh-ost, which work by making a shadow copy of the existing table, copying everything over and then switching tables. For 1TB table, it means using 2TB of space. On {{central}} cluster where this table is located we currently have enough space:

{noformat}root@d2:~# df -h /mysql/
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/md0        6.8T  3.3T  3.2T  51% /mysql{noformat}

If we reach a situation where we don’t have enough space, it means expanding disk (in case of EBS) or rebuilding the whole cluster if using NVME ephemeral storage. 
In terms of time to finish the operation, on a busy cluster like {{central}}, I'd estimate approximately one week for 1TB. This is because we can go faster at night when load drops, during the day gh-ost progress is close to zero.
